dish: classic French haute cuisine — Ostbelgien's Michelin-starred table since 1977
w: The Pankert family's hotel-restaurant in the middle of St. Vith has held a Michelin star continuously since the 1970s (his father Arno once held two). Third-generation chef Eric Pankert cooks classical French with modern accents; it also scores 15.5/20 in Gault&Millau — the blue-chip fine-dining address of the German-speaking Community.

dish: French tradition with Asian precision — a Michelin-starred tasting menu
w: Ricarda Grommes opened Quadras at the roundabout on Malmedyer Straße in 2016 and won a Michelin star in 2020 (plus 15/20 Gault&Millau), making St. Vith a two-star town. Her cooking moves between French tradition and Asian precision, built on regional produce with exotic touches.

dish: French classics with surprising Asian accents (Gault&Millau 14/20)
w: Eupen's top-rated modern table, scoring 14/20 in Gault&Millau: French classics lifted with Asian accents, served in a warm room with a summer terrace. The Grenz-Echo's annual Gault&Millau round-up lists it among the province's best.

dish: Zeeland mussels in a creamy curry sauce; Ondenval trout à la meunière
w: A Michelin Bib Gourmand in Eupen with the feel of a cosy German Stube. Chef Daniel works fine regional produce into French staples — Zeeland mussels in creamy curry, Ondenval trout à la meunière with almonds and apples — and sells his own jam and limoncello. Good cooking, fair prices.

The dining room of a hotel on Bütgenbach's market square, awarded a Gault&Millau toque (13/20) and listed in the Michelin guide. Modern, well-travelled seasonal menus (a 4-course dinner and a 7-course fine-dining menu) make it the fine table of the southern lake country.

dish: rognons de veau à la liégeoise; Bleu-Belge steak — Michelin Bib Gourmand
w: In a restored 200-year-old farm at Eynatten, Angela and Frédéric Noël cook a seasonal French-Belgian menu that changes monthly — Bleu-Belge steak, pot-au-feu, Liège-style veal kidneys. A Michelin Bib Gourmand and a Gault&Millau address right on the German border.

A well-regarded Eupen restaurant scoring 13.5-14/20 in Gault&Millau and listed in the Michelin guide — a refined, seasonal French kitchen that rounds out the capital's fine-dining bench alongside Couleur Rouge.

dish: Wild (game from the Fagnes) and seasonal moor-country cooking
w: The restaurant of the historic 1811 moor inn on the Hohes Venn, 'das Venn im Blick, das Wild auf dem Teller' as the Grenz-Echo put it — strongly seasonal regional cooking with game to the fore, part brasserie, bakery and beer hall, a classic stop on a Fagnes walk.

dish: Eupen Pils and craft ales brewed in-house, with a summer Biergarten
w: A nano-brewery Maurice Néau built into an old workshop in central Eupen in 2018 — up to 26 different beers, from Pilsner and IPA to Belgian and experimental ales, and 'ein Eupen Pils, in Eupen gebraut' once more. Brewing courses, tastings and a beer garden open May-September; BRF has covered it as the town's craft-beer revival.

dish: Reisfladen (Rhenish rice tart) and Belgian cream tarts
w: A family Bäckerei-Konditorei run by master baker Christoph Kelleter, on the 'Made in Ostbelgien' regional-producers roster. The café (50-plus seats) serves the border region's signature Reisfladen (rice tart) alongside Belgian cream specialities like apple-cinnamon and pineapple-nougat tarts.

Egidio Panciera's ice-cream café on Eupen's market square — BRF once reported it served 'the world's second-best ice cream', and on a warm day it sells up to 100 Spaghetti-Eis. House gelato and unusual sorbets (an Isabella-grape sorbet among them); the inventor of Spaghetti-Eis himself has dropped by.

A well-known Eupen friterie for the Belgian national dish done properly — double-fried frites and loaded sandwiches — ranked in the top ten of the Verviers district when the regional press ran its Fritten dossier.

dish: seasonal Belgian-French menu (frog legs, scallops, game) for every budget
w: Brothers Roger and Alain London opened Alt Keris in 1997 in a former café building on Kelmis's main street, in the northernmost town of the DG. The Grenz-Echo's 'Mahlzeit' column praised its versatile, something-for-every-budget Belgian-French menu — frog legs and scallops to game and steaks.

dish: Belgian brasserie classics (moules-frites) in a vaulted town-hall cellar
w: An atmospheric café-brasserie in the vaulted cellar beneath Eupen's historic town hall, with two terraces looking onto the church and market square. Belgian-French brasserie cooking — moules-frites and the like — served continuously from morning to late.
